newsitem.title: INDIA: India sets up panel to study fall in crude output.
newsitem.headline: India sets up panel to study fall in crude output.

text.p: India on Thursday set up a high level committee to examine the reasons for drop in crude oil output from offshore oilfields of the state-run Oil and Natural Gas Corp (ONGC).
A petroleum ministry statement said the committee, announced by Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda, will be headed by K.Narayanan, a renowned geologist.
The committee will also propose a strategy and rectification measures for the oilfields.

Finance Minister P. Chidambaram told a business editors' meeting on Tuesday the country's 1996/97 (April-March) oil output was expected to dip to 32 million tonnes (around 640,000 barrels per day) against an earlier estimate of 33.7 million tonnes (some 674,000 bpd) for the period.
He said the oil import bill for the same period was now estimated at $9.0 billion against a previously calculated $7.8 billion, due to hardening of world crude prices.
Junior Petroleum Minister T.R.Baalu on Wednesday said the decline in crude oil output was due to unexpected behaviour of the oil wells and a very high gas-oil ratio.
He said gas in the wells had come up beyond the normal level and separating gas from oil was not yielding the desired results.

Deve Gowda told parliament deputies on Thursday that India's oilpool account deficit -- the money refunded by the government to oil companies to make up for subsidised prices -- was expected at 155 billion rupees in 1996/97 (April-March) against 57 billion in 1995/96.
He asked the deputies to suggest a strategy to reduce the deficit and to ensure that there was no disruption in supply of kerosene, diesel and other petroleum products.
Deve Gowda said the downstream state-owned firms will be encouraged to enter into oil exploration.
